entries.title: Mayor announces $4.2 million emergency repair plan
entries.content:
Speaking at the site on Main Street, the mayor announced a $4.2 million emergency plan to replace the broken main and the half mile of 1931 cast iron pipe around it.

The utility director said the section that failed was on the city's replacement list for 2028. The plan brings that work forward, with crews starting tomorrow and Main Street expected to reopen in stages over the next three weeks.

The boil-water notice for downtown and Riverside stays in place until test results come back clean, which the utility expects by Thursday. Businesses with water damage can apply for help through the city's small business relief fund from Monday.
entries.author: carol

breakout.title: Mayor announces $4.2 million emergency repair plan
breakout.content:
The city will spend $4.2 million to replace the water main that burst under Main Street on Tuesday morning, along with half a mile of aging pipe around it, Mayor Elena Park announced Tuesday evening.

Standing in front of the fenced-off crater near 4th Street, Park said the money would come from the city's emergency reserve and that work would begin Wednesday morning. The repairs were not due to start until 2028.

We can't keep patching pipes that were laid before anyone on this street was born. This one gave us no warning, and the next one won't either.

Mayor Elena Park

A pipe nearly a century old

The main that failed is a 24-inch cast iron line installed in 1931. Utility director Marcus Webb said inspectors flagged the downtown section as high risk in a 2023 survey, but it sat behind two other projects on the capital plan.

Webb said the break most likely started as a small crack that widened as pressure rose during the morning peak. By the time crews shut the valves on either side, around 9:40 a.m., the escaping water had undermined roughly 60 feet of road surface.

The new plan replaces the failed section and the neighboring pipe between 2nd and 6th streets with ductile iron, which the utility has used for all new mains since the early 2000s.

What it means for downtown

Main Street will reopen in stages over the next three weeks. The block between 3rd and 5th will stay closed to traffic until the road is rebuilt, while the outer blocks should reopen to one lane of traffic by the weekend. The 12 and 14 buses will continue detouring via Oak Avenue, and the Main Street light rail stop remains closed.

At least six businesses reported water damage, including the Main Street Diner and Corner Books. The city's small business relief fund will take applications from Monday, with grants of up to $15,000 for cleanup and lost stock.

Dana Ortiz, who has run the diner for 17 years, spent the afternoon pumping water out of her basement. "We'll be closed the rest of the week at least," she said. "I'm glad they're fixing it properly this time, but I'd have liked it done before it came through my floor."

Boil-water notice stays in place

The boil-water notice for downtown and the Riverside neighborhood remains in effect. Residents should bring tap water to a rolling boil for at least one minute before drinking it, cooking with it or using it to brush their teeth. The utility expects test results to come back clean by Thursday.

Bottled water is available at the Central Library parking lot until 8 p.m. each day while the notice is in effect. Residents who can't get there can call the city's helpline to arrange a delivery.

The city council is expected to vote next month on whether to bring forward the rest of the downtown pipe replacement program, estimated at $31 million over five years.

posts.title: Friday night games moved as Ingrid soaks the coast
posts.content:
Coaches across the coast scrambled on Thursday to find new dates for Friday's fixtures as Storm Ingrid left pitches under water.

Emergency managers said the worst of the surge should pass by mid-afternoon, but low-lying roads near the harbor will stay flooded through the evening high tide.

Residents in evacuation zones were urged to remain at shelters until officials confirm it is safe to return. Schools will be closed again tomorrow.

The county will review its drainage budget at a special session next week, with several members already calling for faster spending on the Lower Quay outfall.

Business owners along the waterfront spent the morning moving stock upstairs and stacking sandbags against doors.
posts.author: charlotte.pearce

posts.title: Schools close across the county as the storm arrives
posts.content:
Every public school in the county will stay closed on Thursday as the winter storm brings heavy snow and freezing rain across the region, the district said on Wednesday evening.

After-school activities and evening events are canceled, and the district will decide on Friday's schedule by 6 a.m.
